en: My husband wasn't any different. He didn't want to help. But me... I couldn't help feeling bad for Okudera-san.
So ya gave 'im food?
Yes. I knew I would regret it if I did not.
Wait, yer givin' me...?
Yes. It's not much, but please take it. It's good venison.
But what if yer husband finds out?
He won't. It'll be fine.
My thanks for yer kindness.
In return, can I ask you a favor?
Can you... just find out why Okudera-san keeps going after that bear?
Why ya wanna know that?
Ever since that incident nine years ago, there's been something wrong with this village.
You see, everyone used to help each other get by. But now, there's no trust. Only suspicion.
No one can forget the terror they experienced that day.
And unfortunately, Okudera-san became the focus of everyone's fears.
So that's what happened...
Okudera-san rarely opens up to anyone, but for some reason, he seems to have accepted you.
My hope is you might become his friend, and maybe even lift the dark cloud that's been hovering over him for nine long years.
Please try. You would be freeing us from such a dreary state of existence.
Alright. Ain't sure what I can do, but I'll try, ma'am. I'm indebted to ya, after all.
Thank you. Please be careful.
More trouble... Damn that Okudera!
Honey...
Sorry to intrude. But I got a favor to ask.
You're still here? Didn't I tell you to get lost?
Honey, really...
What do you want? If it's food, we're already short. Find your own.
I know ya are. That's why I want to borrow a gun.
I know I'm an outsider. But I feel indebted to Okudera-han for savin' me, and also to you and yer wife. I owe somethin' to the whole village, really.
I also know I'm an amateur, but I just can't take bein' a burden on ya any longer.
Please. Lemme hunt! At the same time, I can protect Okudera-han from Yama-oroshi.
Darling...
The mountain's a far harsher place than you realize, Saejima. Even veteran hunters lose their way in a storm like this.
I'm not going to⑬
See, you don't get it! Or your ego is just huge... If our best trackers have gotten lost chasing quarry into the wild, what makes you think you can do it?
I do know the dangers, Nishina. It's just...
You might know them, but you don't understand them! How could you? You weren't here nine years ago.
Forget about borrowing a gun. Go home and wait for your buddy Okudera to come back from his wild goose chase.
Don't be. It's my fault for not thinkin' this out.
He's just afraid that what happened nine years ago will happen again.
Yeah, when Yama-oroshi attacked the village.
It's not just that. What scares us most is the possibility of death.
But Sakurai-han said no one died nine years ago.
Well, that's...
What are you prattling on about!?
For goodness' sake...
We don't tell outsiders anything!
Saejima, if you have no business here, then scram! Our lives are hard enough without you bothering us!
Wow. You're up and about already?
I feel fine.
Thank you for getting the bait. That was a dangerous job.
Not a big deal.
Tch. If you say so.
We were just talking about Narumi.
He ain't back yet?
No. Based on what you told us, I'd guess he's too wounded to move.
Then I gotta go get 'im.
Why? If you ask me, Narumi's body would make decent bear food... much better than that bait of his that nearly got us all killed!
Sakurai-han, I understand why ya hate the guy. He almost destroyed yer village.
But don't go condemnin' him to die. Evil ain't the way to respond to evil. Least, it shouldn't be.
But⑬
I'm goin'. And to be frank, I don't need yer approval. I'll do what I want.
You're... something else, Saejima-san.
*chuckle*
I don't expect anythin', but if ya could make me one last pack, I'd sure be grateful.
I'll do it. But for you; not for him. I'll be at Okudera's.
"Pride's Toll" was added.
Sorry for what you went through...
Narumi!
So you're alive.
Yeah, haha. Can you believe I look like this after just one hit? What the hell is that creature?
We warned ya; Yama-oroshi ain't no joke. Just survivin' him means you're prob'ly part cat, with nine lives n' all.
Hehe, and I've used up most of my nine lives, I think. I might actually start listening to you, now!
Ya serious?
Yeah; you saved my life! If you hadn't shouted while it was mauling me, I'd be dead.
Honestly, I... I start shaking if I think about it...
...Look, we ain't got time to talk right now. Can ya walk?
Uh, I didn't think so, but maybe...
Ya got to. Bears are out here, thanks to you. Let's go.
This heap?
I found it ten years ago, pretty close to where Okudera was once abandoned by a hunter named Sato.
That mean it's Okudera-han's?
I thought it best to keep it hidden. But now its time has come.
But why would ya do that?
I can explain later. But we need to act <Italic>now</Italic>, and no one else in the village can drive this thing.
So? Are you going to help? I'll understand if you don't want to risk your neck.
I'll do it. If ya think it's the best way to help 'im.
Thank you. We're counting on you to save Okudera.
Do what I can.
(I'm comin' for ya, friend. Yer people care about ya too much to let ya martyr yerself.)
Hey, I've been seeing you around here a lot these days.
I take it you're a big fan of mahjong.
You are?
The name's Sakuragi. Say, do you have any interest in high-stakes matches?
High stakes?
If regular mahjong isn't enough for you, join me. I'll introduce you to a new world of excitement.
Looking for another mark, Sakuragi-san?
Hey, pal, don't believe anything that guy says. He's a cheat. If you take that challenge, he'll burn you for everything you own.
They say he's the unbeatable legend, but that's a load of BS. Trust me on this⑬you'll regret having anything to do with him.
Isn't that right, Sakuragi-san?
Let me disabuse you of your misconception. I'm no cheat. Even if I were cheating, you'd have to catch me in the act to make that claim.
Why, you...!
You're pissed because you lost. But think it over⑬do you really want to waste the rest of your life over hastening this old boy's death?
...Dammit!
Fuck you! My life's already fucked to hell and back, thanks to you!
Heh, sorry, buddy. You must be jinxed to end up mixed up in this nonsense.
Maybe it's a sign you're not blessed with luck. Maybe you shouldn't be playing mahjong after all.
Get out of my way! I got a score to settle with Sakuragi. If you're going to interfere, I'll kick your ass first!
Well. Quite the impressive demonstration. It's obvious you're no stranger to danger.
Your instincts are sharp, and you've got balls. I'd like to see how you play mahjong.
I'll see you around. The name's Shogo Sakuragi. People have also called me the God of Mahjong.
The God of Mahjong?
Overblown, huh? But they say they got no other name to describe me. See you around, bud.
(The God of Mahjong, Shogo Sakuragi...)
Ah, we meet again. Remember me? It's Sakuragi. You helped me out of a tight spot.
Remember what I said before? Come join me if you want to see some excitement.
I'm your man if the penny-ante mahjong you've been playing isn't enough for you.
Each participant posts a winner-take-all stake of 500,000 points in addition to the 25,000 needed to play, for a total of 525,000 points.

Rules are set at the start of the match, choosing either a Quarter or a Half Game. At the end of play, the top player wins the entire pot of two million points. If you quit the game, you forfeit your 500,000-point stake.
So, will you put up the 500,000 points and play with me?
Good. That's good.
I'll take your 500,000 point stake.
Let's begin.
Hold it, hold it. You can't go on without your stake. Do you want to buy 500,000 points worth of mahjong sticks now?
Okay. I'll buy the 500,000 points.
Good. I'll put that up as your stake.
Wait. You don't have enough to buy in. Get enough mahjong sticks together first, all right?
No? Might be a wise decision. But if you change your mind, give me a shout.
Ah, it's been a while. What can I do for you? Are you itching for some high-stakes mahjong?
I hate to admit it, but you dominated the table. I'm not quite the master I thought I was.
Here. Take your two million points.
That was thrilling, though. We should do this again sometime.
Well, that was thrilling. I'll keep your stake of 500,000 points.
I have to say, that was as good as it gets. If you're so inclined, join us again sometime.
Hey now. It's a disgrace and discourteous to quit a game. I'll split up your 500,000-point stake among us.
Yo, play some mahjong with us? No lie, but we're pretty shit at the game.
Okay, let's get started, then!
Actually, I'll pass.
Bummer. Well, if ya change your mind, we'll be here.
Yo, wanna play with us? We're all pretty average players, I'd say.
All right, now we're talkin'! C'mon, let's get this started.
Aw, shoot. Feel free to hit us up when you feel up to it.
Pull up a chair and join us. We're pretty damn good if you're lookin' for some heat.
Right on, bud. Let's get this show on the road.
I have to go. It's the only way.
Yo, there! Are ya talkin' about goin' up the mountain?
Yes, that's right.
S'posed to be dangerous, but ya seem pretty determined. Why're ya goin'?
No reason. I just feel like it.
Ya think I'm some idiot? C'mon, out with it.
Okay, well...
Have you ever heard of the gold stag?
Gold? Nah. Is it around here?
Only according to rumor. It might not even exist, but it's the only chance I have left.
My mother's sick.
We spent what little savings we had going to big hospitals all over.
And still, no one could diagnose her! We were desperate. That's when I heard about the gold stag⑬its meat can cure any disease!
I know, I know. It sounds like a fairy tale.
But I have no other options. And even if it's a one-in-a-million chance...
(Geez. Poor kid.)
Hey, I get it; ya would do anything for yer ma. But think about this⑬what is she gonna do if ya get killed out there?
Look, I don't believe in fairy tales, but I'll take care of this one for ya. The last thing yer ma needs is you puttin' yer life on the line.
Wait, you'll hunt the stag for me?
I'll look for it whenever I happen to be on the mountain. Meanwhile, you'll be down here thinkin' of more practical ways to help yer ma, 'cause this ain't no guarantee. Sound good?
Yes, but... Why would you do this for me?
Ya don't wanna regret anythin' later on. I know that all too well, that's all.
Well. Thank you!
"Hunt a Gold Stag" was added to the list of missions.
So... was the gold stag just a myth after all?
(Should I give 'im the gold stag meat?)
Turns out it's real. Here ya go.
You handed over <Color:8>Gold Stag Meat<Color:Default>.
Oh my gosh! Really...?
Yeah. Go. Take it to yer mother.
Sir, I'm forever indebted to you. Truly.
I feel terrible that you're doing something so dangerous for me. But... you're my only hope.
Oh! Saejima-san!
How's yer mother?
She's getting better! It's a miracle!
You saved her life. Mine too, for that matter. Thank you.
Heh, we'll never really know if it was the meat that healed 'er. But yer welcome.
I'm convinced it was the meat. So, may I offer this to you in gratitude?
You got <Color:8>Goddess of Children Amulet<Color:Default>.
Sure. 'Preciate it.
You were a blessing to us.
Oh! It's you!
Uh, and you're...?
Yeah, it's been a while. You brought my father's time capsule back from the mountain for me.
Ah, that's right. Thought ya were done with the town, though. Why're ya here now?
It's a funny story. See, I study chronic diseases at the university hospital in Tsukimino.
And it turns out, the key I've been seeking all these years is right here on the mountain.
What key?
Mushrooms. I found a dried-up mushroom in my father's time capsule.
It's poisonous, but it also contains a substance that may be an effective control for a disease I'm studying.
Hell of a coincidence.
Isn't it!? The only problem is, the mushroom I have is not a large enough sample, and⑬
Let me guess. Ya want me to fetch ya more of that type of mushroom.
Precisely. I'm sorry to impose on you again, but... I'll pay you, of course.
Well... okay. Sounds like you're workin' on somethin' good for society.
Great! Science will thank you.
I only need three of them, so...
Alright, three toxic mushrooms. If I find 'em, I'll bring 'em here.
"Get Toxic Shrooms" was added to the list of missions.
I still need three toxic mushrooms for my studies.
